findings.reason: lib/yargs-parser.ts:225 now calls only isUnknownOptionAsArg(arg). isUnknownOption (972-989) returns !hasFlagsMatching, and every pattern there starts with ^-+, so a word like 'command' is reported unknown. The branch is taken before the halt-at-non-option break at 397-399, so later flags get parsed instead of staying in _.
findings.claim: Removing the /^-/ guard makes plain positionals count as unknown options when unknown-options-as-args is on, so they go to pushPositional before the halt-at-non-option branch and parsing no longer stops at the first non-option.
findings.evidence: Line 225 is now `if (arg !== '--' && isUnknownOptionAsArg(arg)) { pushPositional(arg)`. `isUnknownOption` (lines 972-989) returns `!hasFlagsMatching(...)`, and every pattern it checks starts with `^-+`, so a word with no leading dash matches none and is reported unknown (true). This branch comes before `else if (configuration['halt-at-non-option']) { notFlags = args.slice(i); break }` at lines 397-399, so that branch is never reached for positionals. Example: `['foo','--known','x']` with `string:['known']` and both settings on used to give `_:['foo','--known','x']`; it now gives `_:['foo']` and `known:'x'`.
